title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 127 (Punishment for failure to distribute dividends)

content.overview: Where a dividend has been declared by a company but has not been paid or the warrant in respect thereof has not been posted within thirty days from the date of declaration to any shareholder entitled to the payment of the dividend, every director of the company shall, if he is knowingly a party to the default, be punishable with imprisonment which may extend to two years and with fine which shall not be less than one thousand rupees for every day during which such default continues and the company shall be liable to pay simple interest at the rate of eighteen per cent. per annum during the period for which such default continues. Section 127 lists exceptions where no offence is committed.
content.glance: Dividend must be paid or the warrant posted within thirty days of declaration; knowing directors and the company face the statutory consequences, subject to listed exceptions.
content.study:
## Section 127 — Punishment for failure to distribute dividends

**Default.** Declared dividend not paid, or warrant not posted, within thirty days of declaration.

**Consequences.** Every director knowingly a party to the default: imprisonment up to two years and fine not less than one thousand rupees for every day of default. Company: simple interest at eighteen per cent per annum for the default period.

**Exceptions (proviso).** Include where the dividend could not be paid by reason of any law; where a shareholder has given directions which cannot be complied with; where there is a dispute regarding the right to receive the dividend; where the dividend has been lawfully adjusted against any sum due from the shareholder; and where the failure is not due to any default on the part of the company.

Declaration itself is section 123.

This note is a focused study aid; the topic remains under source and current-law review.

hypotheticals.question: Is cash-flow difficulty alone an exception under section 127?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. The proviso lists specific exceptions. Convenience or cash-flow shortage is not itself a listed exception.
